summary: Cryptominer disguised as lodash executes on require via obfuscated bundle
details: Package publishes a verbatim lodash v4.18.1 README and lodash-related keywords, but the declared main entry dist/common-js.js is a heavily obfuscated bundle (javascript-obfuscator rotating string array plus an embedded ~55KB encoded blob consistent with a WebAssembly hasher). The bundle contains stratum mining client strings ('stratum', 'hashrate', 'nonce', 'difficulty', 'worker', 'WebSocket', 'pool'), a hardcoded ws://pool destination, and a http://127.0.0.1:8080/ loopback control reference; @noble/ciphers AES-GCM is bundled to protect pool traffic. On require('@finaxis/common-js') the obfuscated IIFE runs at import time, connecting the installer's process to a remote stratum pool and executing mining jobs issued by that pool on the installer's CPU. The package name, README, and keywords are a deliberate cover story unrelated to the shipped code.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
